text:
The Blue Jackets' injury list is starting to write their season. Conor Garland is on injured reserve, week to week with an upper-body injury, and Sean Monahan is day to day with one of his own. That is two-thirds of a line gone from a team that can't spare much scoring, and Columbus has now lost four straight (0-4-0), outscored 16-7. Saturday's 4-3 loss to Philadelphia, after leading by two, stung more than most.

At 7-11-0 with 14 points, the Jackets are near the bottom of the East, and our playoff odds have them at 8%. The frustrating part is that the play is closer than the record: 49% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances). They've just scored 8.8 fewer goals than those chances usually produce. That is the biggest single reason the standings look like this.

What's working is easy to find. Zach Werenski keeps scoring, and his pair with Damon Severson has outscored teams 13-7 in more than 250 minutes. Cam Talbot is on a heater: .930 with 6.2 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. The Charlie Coyle, Mathieu Olivier and Cole Sillinger line drives play.

What we'd watch: whether Adam Fantilli's line can carry more of the scoring while the injured heal, before the gap gets too wide to close.
